read: Pick components by metadata (whenToUse / whenNotToUse). Props, variants and tokens are extracted from source and authoritative. See USAGE.md for the rules.

components.description: Static status label. Not interactive: use `Button` for actions.
usage: Short status or category text (one or two words), never a sentence.

metadata.summary: A small static label for a status or category, such as "Active" or "Draft".
whenToUse: Showing a row status in a DataTable cell.
Tagging an item with a short category or plan name.
Flagging something as new, deprecated or failed, with variant="destructive" for errors.
whenNotToUse: Anything clickable: use Button with variant="outline" or "ghost".
Sentences or explanations: use plain text or CardDescription.

alternatives.when: Pressing the element should do something.

antiPatterns: Attaching onClick to a Badge; it is not focusable or keyboard accessible, so use Button.
Long text in a badge; keep it to one or two words.
accessibility: Renders a plain <span>, read as inline text.
If color alone carries meaning (red vs grey), the text must also say it ("Failed", not just a red dot).

components.description:
Button on React Aria Components. Use `onPress` / `isDisabled`, not
`onClick` / `disabled`. For links styled as buttons, put the `button()`
recipe on a React Aria `Link` or your router's link.
usage: One primary button per view or section; the rest secondary, outline or ghost.
Not for navigation: links that look like buttons use the `button()` recipe on a link.

metadata.summary: A pressable control that runs an action, such as saving a form or opening a dialog.
whenToUse: Submitting or saving a form.
Starting an action on the current page, such as opening a modal or deleting an item.
A destructive action, with variant="destructive" (often followed by a ConfirmDialog).
Low-emphasis actions in toolbars or table rows, with variant="ghost" or "outline".
whenNotToUse: Navigating to another page: put the button() recipe on a router link or React Aria Link.
Showing a status or category: use Badge.
Toggling an on/off setting: use Checkbox.

alternatives.when: The action is destructive and needs an explicit "are you sure" step.
The element only shows a label and does nothing when clicked.

antiPatterns: Using onClick or disabled; use onPress and isDisabled, which React Aria handles for touch, keyboard and mouse.
Wrapping a Button in an <a> for navigation; style the link itself with the button() recipe.
Several primary buttons in one section; keep one primary and make the rest secondary, outline or ghost.
Changing colors through className; override the --button-primary-* or semantic tokens instead.
accessibility: Handles keyboard activation, focus-visible ring and the disabled state for you.
An icon-only button needs an aria-label.

components.import: import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter } from '@brafols/ui'
components.description: Presentational container. Compose with CardHeader / CardContent / CardFooter.

metadata.summary: A bordered surface that groups related content, built from CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent and CardFooter.
whenToUse: Grouping a form or a settings section on a page.
A tile in a grid of items, such as plans, projects or stats.
Framing a small self-contained flow, such as sign-in.
whenNotToUse: Content that must block the page until the user acts: use Modal.
A list with no items: use EmptyState (inside a Card if the section needs the frame).
Tabular data: use DataTable, optionally inside a Card.

alternatives.when: The content needs the user’s full attention and blocks the page.
The section exists but has nothing to show yet.

antiPatterns: Putting content directly in Card and expecting padding; Card has none, so wrap content in CardContent or CardHeader.
Restyling the surface with bg-*/border-* classes; override --card or --border tokens instead.
Nesting cards inside cards for spacing; use layout (grid/gap) inside one CardContent.
Adding pt-6 to a CardContent or CardFooter with no CardHeader above it; they already pad their top when they are the first child.
accessibility: Purely presentational; CardTitle renders an <h3>, so make sure that heading level fits the page outline.
metadata.example:
<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Billing</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Your plan renews on 1 November.</CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent className="grid gap-4">…</CardContent>
  <CardFooter className="justify-end">
    <Button>Update plan</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>

metadata.summary: A labelled checkbox for a yes/no choice or for picking items from a set.
whenToUse: Accepting terms or opting into emails in a form.
Choosing several items from a short list.
A "select all" control, with isIndeterminate when only some items are selected.
whenNotToUse: Picking exactly one of many options: use Select.
Running an action immediately on press: use Button.

alternatives.when: Only one option can be chosen.

antiPatterns: Reading event.target.checked in onChange; onChange receives the boolean directly.
Using a Checkbox without its label prop and adding a separate text node; pass label so the whole row is clickable and named.
accessibility: Renders a real checkbox input with its label, so it is keyboard and screen-reader accessible.
Announces the indeterminate state; the caller must still describe what "select all" covers.
metadata.example: <Checkbox label="Email me about new classes" isSelected={optIn} onChange={setOptIn} />

components.description: "Are you sure?" prompt built on `Modal`. The confirm button is destructive by default.
usage: Only for destructive or irreversible actions; don't confirm routine saves.
The confirm label names the action ("Delete member"), never "OK" or "Yes".

own.name: confirmLabel
own.doc: Defaults to a localised generic label; prefer a label that names the action.

own.name: pendingLabel
own.doc: Shown on the confirm button while `isPending`. Defaults to a localised label.

own.name: isPending
own.doc: Disables both buttons and shows `pendingLabel` while the action runs.

metadata.summary: A modal "are you sure?" step with a cancel and a confirm button, destructive by default.
whenToUse: Before deleting, removing or revoking something that can’t be undone.
Before an irreversible action with side effects for other people, such as cancelling a booking.
whenNotToUse: Routine saves or reversible changes: just do them, and offer undo if needed.
Collecting input before acting: use Modal with a form.

alternatives.when: The step needs more than a yes/no, such as a reason or a form.

antiPatterns: Confirm labels like "OK" or "Yes"; name the action ("Delete member").
Closing the dialog before the action finishes; keep it open with isPending until the request settles.
Using confirmVariant="primary" for a destructive action; leave the destructive default.
Passing translated "Cancel" or "Working…" labels by hand; the defaults follow React Aria’s locale, so pass only labels that differ.
accessibility: Built on Modal: focus trap, Escape to cancel, and focus returns to the trigger.
While isPending, both buttons are disabled and clicking the backdrop does nothing.
Default cancel, confirm and pending labels are localised (en, es, ca) from React Aria’s locale; the caller still provides a confirmLabel naming the action.
metadata.example:
<ConfirmDialog
  open={isOpen}
  title="Delete this member?"
  message="Their history stays, but they lose access right away."
  confirmLabel="Delete member"
  isPending={remove.isPending}
  onConfirm={() => remove.mutate(member.id)}
  onCancel={close}
/>

components.description:
Read-only data table on React Aria's `Table` (keyboard navigation, row
headers). No sorting or pagination yet. The first column is the row header.
usage: Put the column that identifies the row (name, title) first.

own.name: aria-label
own.doc: Accessible name of the table. Defaults to a localised name.

own.name: emptyMessage
own.doc: Shown when `data` is empty. Defaults to a localised message.

metadata.summary: A read-only, keyboard-navigable table rendered from columns and rows of data.
whenToUse: Lists of records with several comparable fields, such as members, invoices or bookings.
Admin views where people scan rows and compare columns.
whenNotToUse: A handful of items with one or two fields: use a simple list or Cards.
No rows yet: DataTable shows emptyMessage, but for a whole empty section use EmptyState.
Sorting or pagination: not supported yet, so request it in the library instead of wrapping another table.

alternatives.when: Items are few and each needs its own actions or rich content.
The section has no data and needs a call to action.

antiPatterns: Leaving aria-label at its generic localised default; name what the table lists ("Members").
Putting the identifying column (name, title) anywhere but first; the first column is the row header.
Formatting values inline in data; use a column render function, for example a Badge for status.
accessibility: Built on React Aria Table: grid semantics, arrow-key navigation and row headers.
The default name and empty message are localised (en, es, ca) from React Aria’s locale.
The caller provides the accessible name (aria-label) and readable cell content.
metadata.example:
<DataTable
  aria-label="Members"
  keyField="id"
  data={members}
  columns={[
    { key: 'name', header: 'Name' },
    { key: 'email', header: 'Email' },
    { key: 'status', header: 'Status', render: (v) => <Badge>{String(v)}</Badge> },
  ]}
/>

components.description: Placeholder for a collection with no items.

metadata.summary: A centered message for a list or section that has no items yet, with an optional action.
whenToUse: A list, table or dashboard section with no data yet.
Search or filter results that came back empty.
whenNotToUse: While data is loading: use Spinner.
Errors from a failed request: show an error message with a retry action instead of "nothing here".

alternatives.when: The data is still loading.

antiPatterns: Showing EmptyState before the first load finishes; show Spinner until the request settles.
A vague title like "No data"; say what is missing ("No members yet").
accessibility: The title renders as an <h3>; make sure that fits the page heading outline.
metadata.example:
<EmptyState
  title="No members yet"
  description="Invite your first member to get started."
  action={<Button onPress={openInvite}>Invite member</Button>}
/>

components.description:
Bare styled input for building custom fields. Prefer `TextField`, which
wires label, description and error for you.
usage: Only when composing a custom field; always pair it with a Label.

metadata.summary: A bare styled text input for composing a custom field.
whenToUse: Building a custom field layout that TextField can’t express, paired with Label.
whenNotToUse: Any ordinary text, email or password field: use TextField, which wires label, description and error.
Numbers: use NumberField. Search boxes: use SearchField.

alternatives.when: Almost always: a labelled single-line field with error handling.
The value is numeric.
The field filters or searches.

antiPatterns: Using Input without a Label; every input needs an accessible name.
Rebuilding error and description handling around Input; use TextField.
accessibility: Provides no label, description or error wiring; the caller must link a Label via htmlFor/id.

components.description: Styled label. Inside a React Aria field it links up automatically.

metadata.summary: A styled form label that links to its control automatically inside React Aria fields.
whenToUse: Labelling a control in a custom field built from Input or other React Aria parts.
whenNotToUse: Library fields (TextField, Select, NumberField, …): pass their label prop instead.

alternatives.when: A standard labelled text field is enough.

antiPatterns: Adding a Label next to a library field that already has a label prop, which double-labels it.
Using Label as general-purpose text styling; use typography classes on the right element instead.
accessibility: Outside a React Aria field, link it to its control with htmlFor/id.

components.description: Modal dialog with focus trap, focus restore, scroll lock and Escape to close.
usage: For short, focused tasks that block the page (an edit form, a decision); not for long content.

own.name: aria-label
own.doc: Accessible name when there is no visible `title`.

own.name: isDismissable
own.doc: Close when the backdrop is clicked. Escape always closes.

metadata.summary: A dialog over the page that traps focus until the user finishes or dismisses it.
whenToUse: A short edit form opened from a list or detail view.
A focused decision that needs more than yes/no.
whenNotToUse: A plain "are you sure?" before a destructive action: use ConfirmDialog.
Long or primary content: give it its own page.
Grouping content on a page: use Card.

alternatives.when: The step is only a yes/no confirmation.
The content can live on the page without blocking it.

antiPatterns: No title and no aria-label; the dialog then has no accessible name.
Toggling open without handling onClose; Escape and backdrop clicks call onClose, so update your state there.
Setting the theme on an inner element; modals render on <body>, so data-theme belongs on <html>.
accessibility: Handles the focus trap, focus restore, scroll lock and Escape to close.
Uses title as the accessible name; without a title, pass aria-label.

components.description:
Numeric field. Value-based numeric `onChange`. Pass
`formatOptions={{ useGrouping: false }}` for year-like values so `2024`
isn't shown as `2,024`.

metadata.summary: A labelled field for numeric values, with locale-aware formatting and parsing.
whenToUse: Quantities, prices, ages or counts.
Years, with formatOptions={{ useGrouping: false }} so 2024 isn’t shown as 2,024.
whenNotToUse: Codes that only look numeric (postcodes, phone numbers, IDs): use TextField.
Choosing from a few fixed values: use Select.

alternatives.when: The value is digits but not a number you calculate with.
Only a few specific values are allowed.

antiPatterns: Parsing a string from onChange; it already receives a number (NaN when empty).
Formatting years with default options, which adds a thousands separator.
accessibility: Handles the label, description and error wiring, plus arrow-key stepping.

components.description:
Search field. Value-based `onChange`; shows a clear button while it has a
value. Give it a `label` or an `aria-label`.

own.name: clearLabel
own.doc: Accessible name of the clear button. Defaults to a localised label.

metadata.summary: A search input with a clear button that appears while it has a value.
whenToUse: Filtering a list or table as the user types.
A search box above results.
whenNotToUse: Ordinary form text: use TextField.

alternatives.when: The input is form data, not a query.

antiPatterns: No label and no aria-label; a placeholder is not an accessible name.
Running a network request on every keystroke; debounce the value from onChange.
accessibility: Escape clears the field, and the clear button is labelled (a localised default from React Aria’s locale, or clearLabel).
The caller provides label or aria-label.
metadata.example: <SearchField aria-label="Search members" placeholder="Name or email" value={query} onChange={setQuery} />

usage: For 4+ options; with 2–3 options a set of buttons or checkboxes is often clearer.

metadata.summary: A labelled dropdown for picking one option from a list, built as a listbox in a popover.
whenToUse: Picking one value from four or more options, such as a plan, role or country.
Form fields where the options are known up front.
whenNotToUse: Two or three options: buttons or checkboxes are usually clearer.
Picking several options: use Checkbox items.
Free text or long searchable lists: use TextField or SearchField.

alternatives.when: Several options can be selected.
The list is long enough that people need to search it.

antiPatterns: Treating it as a native <select> (value/onChange, userEvent.selectOptions); use selectedKey/onSelectionChange, and in tests click the trigger and then the option.
Passing options without stable value strings; value is the key emitted by onSelectionChange.
accessibility: Handles listbox semantics, typeahead, keyboard navigation and focus management.
The popover renders on <body>, so the theme must be set on <html>.
metadata.example:
<Select
  label="Plan"
  placeholder="Choose a plan"
  options={[{ value: 'monthly', label: 'Monthly' }, { value: 'yearly', label: 'Yearly' }]}
  selectedKey={plan}
  onSelectionChange={(key) => setPlan(String(key))}
/>

own.name: label
own.doc: Accessible name announced to screen readers. Defaults to a localised label.

metadata.summary: An indeterminate loading indicator announced to screen readers.
whenToUse: A section or page is waiting for data.
A short wait with no known progress.
whenNotToUse: A button’s own pending state: disable the Button and change its label (as ConfirmDialog does).
Loaded data that came back empty: use EmptyState.

alternatives.when: Loading has finished and there is nothing to show.

antiPatterns: Several spinners on one screen for the same request; show one for the region that is loading.
Leaving the generic localised default label when the context matters ("Loading invoices").
accessibility: Renders role="status" with an accessible label, localised (en, es, ca) from React Aria’s locale by default.
The caller can make the label specific.

components.description: Multi-line text field. Value-based `onChange`. `error` marks it invalid.

metadata.summary: A labelled multi-line text field with description and error built in.
whenToUse: Free-form text longer than one line, such as messages, notes or descriptions.
whenNotToUse: Single-line values such as names or emails: use TextField.

alternatives.when: The value fits on one line.

antiPatterns: Reading event.target.value in onChange; it receives the string directly.
Showing validation messages outside the field; pass error so it is announced and linked.
accessibility: Handles label, description and error wiring, including aria-invalid.

components.description: Single-line text field. Value-based `onChange`. `error` marks it invalid.

metadata.summary: A labelled single-line text field with description and error built in.
whenToUse: Names, emails, passwords, URLs and other single-line text.
Any form field that shows a validation error.
whenNotToUse: Multi-line text: use TextArea.
Numbers you calculate with: use NumberField.
Search and filter boxes: use SearchField.

alternatives.when: The text can span several lines.
The value is a number.
The field filters or searches.

antiPatterns: Reading event.target.value in onChange; it receives the string directly.

Building a field from Input + Label + a

for errors; TextField already wires them accessibly.
Using placeholder as the label; always pass label (or aria-label).
accessibility: Handles the label, description and error wiring, including aria-invalid when error is set.
Provide autocomplete hints (autoComplete="email") where they apply.
metadata.example: <TextField label="Email" type="email" autoComplete="email" value={email} onChange={setEmail} error={errors.email} />
